deep.reconstruction:
The page has drawings only. It has no running text apart from Greek letters and point labels. The verso is a reused 1982 Cadarache computer listing, which is irrelevant. Read with the previous page (duality of triangles in a real projective plane X and its dual, and orientations) and the next page (exceptional facets, multiple vertices, a 'branche principale' δ, concurrent branches of L), the sketches are working pictures for the combinatorial topology of pseudoline systems in the real projective plane P²(R).

(1) Upper left: a rectangle cut by a horizontal segment into a region α above and β below, with faint rounded outlines. This is most plausibly a fundamental domain for P² or the Möbius band (a strip whose ends are identified with a flip), split by one pseudoline into two cells. It echoes the α/β labels of the oriented frames on the previous page.

(2) Upper middle: the same strip with a lens (ellipse) inscribed and several strands crossing between the top and bottom edges. Arrow-like ticks on the boundary indicate gluing directions. This looks like an arrangement of pseudolines drawn in a strip or wiring-diagram model, with the ellipse a distinguished closed curve, probably a conic or a pseudoline seen in a disc model.

(3) Lower left: two such rectangles stacked. Boundary points are labelled u', a, u on the left and u', a', u on the right, with repeated labels u, u', a, a' on the second block. This records edge identifications: points with the same or primed labels are glued, possibly with a twist. Braided strands cross in narrow zones between and inside the blocks. Plausible readings are a sweep or isotopy of an arrangement (two successive 'time slices' of a wiring diagram) or a two-sheeted picture such as S² covering P². Each slice contains an ellipse running from a to a'.

(4) Lower middle: the same braided strands drawn inside an oval or lens, i.e. a disc model of P² with antipodal identification of the boundary. The two lens vertices are marked points.

(5) Bottom left, in colour: a red horizontal line and two red vertical lines. Several yellow-green curves converge to a black point on the first red vertical, where they meet the red horizontal; a short blue mark sits near the point. Hatching marks one side of the curves, and small ticks mark crossings. This matches the figure and the text of the next page (dated 1.1.84). There, a multiple vertex lies on an exceptional facet. One chooses a principal branch δ of L, and the other branches of L are concurrent at a point on K_0. Red appears to correspond to the lines D or K and green to branches of L, with hatching indicating the facets F, F'.

Overall purpose: visual exploration of how pseudolines or branches sit near multiple points and exceptional facets, and of models (strip, disc) of P² used to draw arrangements and their deformations.
errors: No checkable statements on the page. The drawings are exploratory; the edge labels (u, u', a, a') are not consistently paired, so the intended gluing cannot be fully determined.
